expectations.evidence: The helper is itself filed as a finding in the impact-ordered list: REVIEW.md:94-104 '### 7. chunked_call / mget_dynamic copy every chunk before unpacking — lines 134-150, 152-167', asserting 'The current form allocates a 256-slot table per chunk and does 256 #chunk + 1 length operations ... plus the GC pressure' and that chunked_call 'does not' need its copy. expectations.text: addresses-multikey-coordination-cost: the review addresses the coordination cost of this 14-key script on default flags (io vs shard-local) and the --lock_on_hashtags trade-off
expectations.evidence: --lock_on_hashtags is never mentioned (grep returns nothing), so the trade-off is absent. The review's foundational claim inverts the actual default-flag behaviour: REVIEW.md:7 'One hashtag = one shard = one proactor thread. Every key this script touches hashes to the same slot, so all of its work runs on 1 of the 4 proactor threads.' On Dragonfly v1.34.0 default flags a hashtag is not a placement/lock unit, so a 24+n-key script is io-coordinated across shards, not shard-local; findings 1-9 and measurement item 4 ('one proactor pinned, three idle', :128) are all built on that unevidenced premise. The io vs shard-local distinction is never named.

expectations.text: claims-carry-dragonfly-evidence: every performance claim names Dragonfly-specific evidence (a measurement run, INFO/eval coordination counters, SCRIPT LATENCY, or a Dragonfly v1.34.0 doc/source citation)
expectations.evidence: The quantitative claims are asserted with no measurement, counter or citation: 'At a conservative 3-6 µs of dispatch overhead per call, that alone is 25-50 ms of locked-catalog time' (:24), the squashing/flush-point model in 'Platform facts' (:9), the one-hashtag-one-thread claim (:7), the listpack-vs-skiplist O(N)-per-ZCOUNT branch (:39), and Lua 5.1 string-interning cost (:70). None cites a v1.34.0 run, doc or source. The measurement section proposes counters only after the fact (INFO commandstats, SLOWLOG, ZCARD/OBJECT ENCODING, :125-131), and its premise that 'Dragonfly counts commands dispatched from inside Lua' in commandstats (:125) is itself unverified. No eval coordination counters and no SCRIPT LATENCY.

expectations.text: no-unverified-redis-only-advice: no Redis Functions/FUNCTION migration, no '#!lua flags=no-writes' shebang, no disable-atomicity-for-speed, no client pipelining as the fix for in-script calls, no redis.setresp(3) -- unless backed by Dragonfly evidence
expectations.evidence: Grep for FUNCTION, setresp, '#!lua', 'no-writes' and 'pipelin' finds none of the prohibited recommendations. The single occurrence of pipelining is a comparison, not a proposed fix: 'far more so than the equivalent loop in a pipeline' (:9). No atomicity relaxation is proposed; :28 only argues hoisting the reads loses no ordering or atomicity property.

expectations.text: flags-redundant-writes: the review flags as redundant writes both the delete-and-reinsert of unchanged grants at apply_new_mutable_mailbox_page.lua:612-616 (HDEL/ZREM of grant fields followed by HSET/ZADD of the same rows) and the rewrite at apply_new_mutable_mailbox_page.lua:403-415 of records and grants the script has already compared and proven identical, and states that these writes still cost shard mutations, journal bytes and replica bytes
expectations.evidence: REVIEW.md:45-61 '### 3. Unconditional re-write of grants and records that are already identical — lines 403-414 vs 612-618' covers both halves: 'lines 615 and 618 unconditionally HSET every grant payload and every record JSON back — including the entries the script has just confirmed are byte-identical' and 'the command list does HDEL 7 (line 612) -> ZREM 8 (line 613) -> HSET 7 (line 615) -> ZADD 8 (line 616): a delete-then-reinsert of an unchanged entry'. Costs are stated as 'Four dispatched mutations per unchanged grant instead of zero', dense-hash/zset delete+reinsert churn, and 'Four journal records per unchanged grant replicated to every replica' (:52-55), consistent with platform fact 4 at :10. Matches the input at :612-616 and :403-415; it additionally preserves the half-removed-mailbox reasoning.
